strategic_read: Charon is the healthiest ROLE in the program attached to the deadest INFRASTRUCTURE. Every June artifact shows the same pattern: the operator persona lands real, consumed falsifications (seam leak → allowlist rebuild; empty-kernel finding → CC-1 reframed; stale-address → CC-3 retired; formula-fossil → the '2,351 discoveries' headline retired), while everything automated around it (swarm, loop, cron, backlog) died of empty ticks. The program should draw the obvious conclusion: Charon's value is adversarial judgment applied at decision points, not daemon throughput — revive it as a review gate, not a swarm. Substantively, Charon holds the program's most important unpaid bill: the June reassessment reframed Prometheus around metabolizing/measuring the kill-geometry, and Charon proved the navigable form of that geometry (kill_vector, KillEmbedding/CC-6) was never computed — 0% populated over 5.4M records — while the one live signal (0.725-bit MI) has never faced the right null. The parked navigability pre-test is days of compute and strictly gates the quarter-scale M1 bet; running it should be the first act of any Charon revival, and arguably the program's single highest information-per-dollar move. Second, the census answered what the program's real asset is: not 314K or 367M 'kills' as trainable gradient (those are string labels and shape-class counts, trace-poor), but the graded, replayable fraction — today ~813 rows — plus the discipline primitives (right-null-or-refuse-PASS, allowlist-not-denylist, field-level taint audits) that keep verdicts honest. If the program wants the kill record to become training signal, the work is provenance engineering (store features + formula_version at emit time, compute kill_vector) — exactly the 'data-rich but trace-poor' fix Charon prescribed in May and re-proved in June. Ownership of the frozen Theseus data (F: drive, halted machine) needs an explicit decision before it silently rots.
